key_takeaways: There is no single honest average for a destination wedding, because published figures mix elopements, resort packages and full three-day celebrations.
Our Italy cost guide reports that foreign couples spent an average of €67,000 per wedding in Italy in 2025, citing Florence's Centro Studi Turistici.
Guest count is a major lever: our Italy cost guide (updated November 2026) puts a high-quality wedding at about €800 to €1,200 per guest.
Room blocks, transfers, extra days, VAT, legal paperwork and currency movement often sit outside quoted figures, so ask for each in writing.

faq.q: How much does a destination wedding cost?
faq.a: It depends on the place, the guest count and the number of days. Our Italy cost guide reports that foreign couples spent an average of €67,000 per wedding in Italy in 2025, citing Florence's Centro Studi Turistici. Our Lake Como budget guide estimates €80,000 to €150,000 for a three-day celebration with 60 guests (2026 to 2027), before flights and guest rooms. Treat any average as a starting point, then check what it leaves out.

faq.q: What does a destination wedding cost per guest?
faq.a: Per-guest thinking is the clearest way to compare. Our Italy cost guide (updated November 2026) puts a high-quality wedding at about €800 to €1,200 per guest, which it shows as around €40,000 to €60,000 for 50 guests and €80,000 to €120,000 for 100. Ask whether guest travel and rooms sit inside or on top of any per-guest figure, and decide who pays for them.

faq.q: Is a destination wedding cheaper than a wedding in Australia?
faq.a: Not reliably. An overseas wedding is shaped differently: you may host fewer people at a higher spend per guest, and add costs a wedding at home never has, such as guest rooms, transfers, extra days and vendors who travel with you. Our line-by-line comparison of overseas and home budgets sets the two side by side.

faq.q: Who pays for guests' travel at a destination wedding?
faq.a: There is no fixed rule, so it is your decision. Write down which of flights, rooms, transfers and the welcome dinner you will cover, and which guests book themselves, and put it on your wedding website early. Clear terms help guests plan and help whoever is paying keep the budget steady.

faq.q: Which costs are usually left out of destination wedding averages?
faq.a: Guest rooms and room block terms, transfers, a wet-weather plan, legal paperwork, travel insurance, planner fees, VAT and the movement of the Australian dollar against the contract currency. Our Lake Como budget guide, for example, excludes flights, attire and guest accommodation, and notes that a welcome aperitivo and farewell lunch can add 25 to 40% to the wedding-day total.
